mcq.question: Why report the *median* of several runs?

options.A: It is always the fastest run
options.B: It is cheaper to compute than the mean
options.C: It ignores occasional slow runs caused by the OS or other processes

mcq.explanation: A few interrupted runs pull the mean up but barely move the median.

mcq.question: Doubling the input to the naive duplicate check multiplies the comparisons by about…
mcq.explanation: Comparing every pair is O(n²): n(n−1)/2 comparisons. The hashed version only doubles.

bonus.question: "Premature optimisation is the root of all evil." When is optimising early the right call?
Add a sorted-vector duplicate check (sort, then compare neighbours) and add its operation count to the run output.
